-- Table 2: the leaderboard
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores (
  username     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  total_score  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  badges       TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()

input.new_string:
-- Table 2: the leaderboard (one row per player). Feeds the Leaderboard and
-- PhishSense Masters cards on the home screen. Columns match what server.js
-- writes in POST /api/score and what app.js reads: username, total_score, badges.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaderboard (
  username     TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (char_length(username) BETWEEN 1 AND 20),
  total_score  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  badges       TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',   -- any of 'easy', 'medium', 'hard'
  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Speeds up the two ranking queries (Leaderboard and Masters)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS leaderboard_rank_idx
  ON leaderboard ((cardinality(badges)) DESC, total_score DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS leaderboard_badges_idx ON leaderboard USING GIN (badges);

-- One-time copy: players saved in the old "scores" table move into
-- "leaderboard". Skips anyone already there, so running this again is harmless.
-- The old table is left in place; drop it yourself once you've checked the data.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF to_regclass('public.scores') IS NOT NULL THEN
    INSERT INTO leaderboard (username, total_score, badges, updated_at)
    SELECT left(username, 20), total_score, badges, updated_at FROM scores
    WHERE char_length(username) BETWEEN 1 AND 20
    ON CONFLICT (username) DO NOTHING;
  END IF;
END $$;

content.text:
I've updated the code so the app saves to and reads from a new `leaderboard` table, but the table doesn't exist in your Vultr database yet. I couldn't connect: port 20088 timed out from this computer (public IP `24.125.208.217`), probably because Vultr's Trusted Sources list only allows your deploy server. Your server runs `setup.sql` each time it starts, so the table will be created on your next deploy or restart. To have me create it right now instead, add that IP under **Trusted Sources** in the Vultr panel and ask me to run it.

**The `leaderboard` table** (in `setup.sql`)

| Column | Type | Where the code uses it |
|---|---|---|
| `username` | `TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, 1–20 characters | `POST /api/score` cuts names to 20 characters; both cards show the name |
| `total_score` | `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | Adds up across runs; shown as "pts" on both cards |
| `badges` | `TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` | Any of `easy`, `medium`, `hard`; having all three makes a player a Master |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` | Breaks ties on the Masters list (whoever got there first ranks higher) |

These are the same fields the app sends and reads: `{ username, total_score, badges }`. I also added two indexes to keep the Leaderboard and Masters lists fast.

**Your existing players carry over.** Until now the app stored this data in a table called `scores`. On first run, `setup.sql` copies those rows into `leaderboard`, and later runs skip anyone already there. The old `scores` table is left in place; drop it once you've checked the data.

**Code changes:** every query in `server.js` (saving a score, Leaderboard, Masters, health check, startup) now uses `leaderboard`. Two comments in `public/app.js` were updated to match. No changes to the UI were needed.

**Tested against a local Postgres:**
- A player in the old `scores` table was copied over.
- Points added up correctly across runs, and a repeated badge was stored only once.
- The Leaderboard was sorted by badge count, then score.
- Only players with all three badges appeared on the Masters list.
- On a restart, no rows were duplicated or overwritten.

**Your database password is now in this chat, so consider changing it in Vultr.** I didn't save it to any file. On the server it should only be in `.env` as `DATABASE_URL`, which git already ignores.

Nothing is committed. Want me to commit to `Create_Leaderboard` and open a PR?

content.text:
I created the `leaderboard` table in your Vultr database (`appdb`), and your app's queries work against it. Your live site won't use it until you deploy, because the code still on the server reads and writes `scores`.

**What was already there:** `leaderboard` existed as a read-only view (a saved query over `scores` that added a `rank` column). A table and a view can't share a name, so I dropped the view first. It held no data of its own: `scores` was empty and nothing else depended on the view. I did the drop and the create in one transaction so nothing would be left half-done.

**The table now in your database:**

| Column | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `username` | `text` | Primary key, 1–20 characters |
| `total_score` | `integer` | Required, defaults to `0` |
| `badges` | `text[]` | Required, defaults to `{}` |
| `updated_at` | `timestamptz` | Required, defaults to `now()` |

Two indexes were added to speed up the Leaderboard and Masters lists. These columns match exactly what the app saves and reads.

**Checked against your live database:** I ran the app's own queries inside a transaction and then rolled it back, so no test players were left behind (the table still has 0 rows).
- Saving a score added points up across runs and stored each badge.
- The Leaderboard query returned players sorted by badges, then score.
- The Masters query returned only the player with all three badges.

**Change to `setup.sql`:** it now drops the old view if it finds one before creating the table. Without that, starting the server on a database that still had the view would fail.

**To finish:**
1. Commit and deploy the changes to `server.js`, `setup.sql` and `public/app.js` (nothing is committed yet).
2. Once the new code is running, you can drop the empty `scores` table.
3. You can remove `24.125.208.217` from Trusted Sources in Vultr if you don't need direct access.
4. Consider changing your database password, since it's in this chat. My temporary test scripts are deleted.

Want me to commit to `Create_Leaderboard` and open a PR?
